question: Why do nurses use isolation techniques in the ward?

options.A: To speed up the patient's physical recovery
options.B: To prevent the spread of harmful microorganisms
options.C: To completely cure the underlying disease
options.D: To reduce the cost of hospital medications

explanation: Isolation acts like a shield to stop germs from jumping between patients, staff, and visitors. Great job keeping the ward safe! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h1)

question: Who is protected when a nurse properly uses isolation precautions?

options.A: Only the doctors working in the ward
options.B: Only the patient who is currently sick

explanation: Infection control keeps everyone in the hospital safe and sound—patients, your colleagues, and loved ones who come to visit! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h1)

question: How do isolation methods mainly stop infections from spreading?

options.A: By destroying the causative agent inside the body
options.B: By blocking the mode of transmission
options.C: By eliminating all reservoirs on the hospital ward
options.D: By making the host completely immune to disease

explanation: By putting up physical barriers like gloves, masks, and private rooms, we cut off the path germs use to travel to new hosts. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: In infection control, what do we call a 'reservoir'?

options.A: A person who is immune to the infection
options.B: The route by which a germ leaves the body
options.C: A place where pathogens live and multiply
options.D: The physical barrier used to block germs

explanation: Think of a reservoir as a cozy home for germs. It can be a human, an animal, or even a damp surface where they grow and wait to spread. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which patients should receive Standard Precautions?

options.A: Every patient in the healthcare setting
options.B: Only patients with weak immune systems
options.C: Only patients admitted to the emergency room

explanation: Always treat every patient with Standard Precautions! We treat everyone as if they could carry an infection, keeping both them and us safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: When do you need to add Transmission-Based Precautions?

options.A: When a specific infection is known or suspected
options.B: When the nurse starts a new morning shift
options.C: When standard handwashing fails to work
options.D: When the patient requests a private room

explanation: You add these special precautions (like gowns or masks) on top of standard ones whenever you're dealing with a specific germ. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: What special mask is a must-have for Airborne Precautions?
explanation: Tiny germs floating in the air need an N95 respirator to filter them out before they reach your lungs. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. What do you do right away?
explanation: TB travels easily through tiny air particles. Setting up airborne precautions and grabbing an N95 protects everyone immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: When leaving an isolation room, what is the very first piece of PPE you take off?
explanation: Your gloves have touched the most germs, so they come off first! Always peel them off carefully before touching anything else. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is the order of removing your PPE so important?

options.A: It prevents self-contamination from dirty gear onto clean skin
options.B: It keeps the patient's room looking tidy
options.C: It ensures the equipment can be washed and reused safely
options.D: It saves time during busy hospital shifts

explanation: Following the right steps ensures that the germs on your outer gear don't accidentally end up on your face or skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: What does 'cohorting' mean in the ward?

options.A: Placing patients with the same infection in the same room
options.B: Training new nursing students in isolation procedures
options.C: Sharing medical equipment between different hospital wards
options.D: Moving a patient to a room with negative air pressure

explanation: When single rooms run out, grouping patients with the exact same infection together is a smart way to manage space and safety. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: What special room feature do you need for a patient on Airborne Precautions?
explanation: A negative pressure room pulls air in instead of blowing it out into the hallway when the door opens, trapping germs inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: How do patients in strict isolation often feel emotionally?
explanation: Being cut off from normal human contact behind barriers can make patients feel very lonely and worried. Empathy goes a long way here! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h7)

question: How can you best support a patient feeling down due to isolation?

options.A: Limit all conversations to essential medical updates only
options.B: Keep the room door tightly closed at all hours of the day
options.C: Schedule regular visits and encourage communication with family
options.D: Advise the patient to sleep most of the day away

explanation: A friendly chat, a reassuring smile, and helping them connect with family helps beat the loneliness of isolation. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is considered the single most effective habit to stop the spread of infection?
explanation: Good old handwashing (or using alcohol rub) at the right moments is your absolute best defense against spreading germs! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a correct way to handle hospital waste?

options.A: Sealing biohazard bags securely before carrying them out
options.B: Disposing of sharp needles in designated puncture-proof boxes
options.C: Leaving overfilled waste bags open in the hallway
options.D: Wearing gloves when touching soiled linen or dressings

explanation: Leaving dirty waste bags open in public view is a major hazard! Always seal and dispose of waste safely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h8)
